claim_to_verify: The QIBA CT Tumor Volume Change for Advanced Disease profile (21 July 2022) requires that the same Image Analysis Tool and radiologist measure both timepoints (A.9.1) and 'Shall re-process the first timepoint if it was processed by a different Image Analysis Tool or Radiologist' (A.9.2); it does not say 'version' for the tool. Claims: within-tumour CV 0.141/0.103/0.085 and 95% true-change thresholds 39%/29%/24% for longest diameter 10-34/35-49/50-100 mm (lung). Informative Table B-1: minimum detectable change 28% vs 75% (10-34 mm, same scanner and radiologist, same vs different tool).

The QIBA Small Lung Nodule Volume Assessment and Monitoring in Low Dose CT Screening profile (19 December 2023) requires the same image analysis tool (manufacturer, model, version) at all time points, because 'different versions of the same program or its components may change its performance' (sections 3.10.1-3.10.2); Table 1 CV 0.29 to 0.14 for 6-10 mm nodules.

Two versions of the same lung-nodule volumetry software (LungCARE) gave identical volumes for only 2 of 100 nodules; relative mean between-version variability 1.66% (do not quote the 71%, which compares algorithms).

Prediction churn, the expected fraction of examples whose predicted label changes between two successive models, was defined by Milani Fard et al. (NeurIPS 2016, Eq. 1). Check author order in the official proceedings.
Bansal et al. (AAAI 2019) defined the compatibility score of an update as the fraction of cases the previous model handled correctly that the updated model still handles correctly (Eq. 1).

Srivastava et al. (KDD 2020) named this score backward trust compatibility (BTC) and defined backward error compatibility (BEC), the share of the updated model's errors that the previous model also made; retraining on identical data (25 logistic-regression trials, FICO) already gave BTC 94.5 +/- 1.31% and BEC 78.3 +/- 2.15%.

Shen et al. (CVPR 2020) call recomputing stored gallery features with the new model 'backfilling', and define an empirical compatibility criterion M(new,old) > M(old,old) (Eq. 2) and an update gain normalised by the backfilled new model (Eq. 9).
Träuble et al. (NeurIPS 2021) study whether stored predictions should be replaced ('Replace (a.k.a. backfilling)') when an updated model arrives, measuring negative flips and BTC/BEC.

Ötleş, Denton and Wiens (MLHC 2023, PMLR 219) define a rank-based compatibility measure for continuous risk scores (Eq. 3), with a general form for real-valued labels in the appendix; the measure depends only on orderings.

Echterhoff et al. (Findings of EMNLP 2024, MUSCLE) define per-instance compatibility for continuous evaluation scores: the per-instance score difference between versions, the smoothed negative and positive flip rates, and the mean regression magnitude.

JCGM 200:2012 (VIM 3rd edition, DOI 10.59161/JCGM200-2012) entries: 2.20 repeatability condition (same measurement procedure, same measuring system...); 2.24 reproducibility condition (different locations, operators, measuring systems; Note 1: different measuring systems may use different measurement procedures); 2.47 metrological compatibility of measurement results ('... absolute value of the difference of any pair of measured quantity values from two different measurement results is smaller than some chosen multiple of the standard measurement uncertainty of that difference'). Check that 2012 is still the current edition.

Kessler et al. 2015 (Stat Methods Med Res, QIBA terminology): 2.77 times the within-subject SD is called the repeatability coefficient (RC) under repeatability conditions and the reproducibility coefficient (RDC) under reproducibility conditions.

Raunig et al. 2015 (Stat Methods Med Res): reproducibility variance equals repeatability variance plus between-condition variance, and the conditions can include algorithms; RDC is the least significant difference between two measurements under different conditions.

Athelogou et al. 2016 (QIBA 3A phantom challenge): repeatability coefficient 9.0% with the same algorithm against reproducibility coefficient 22.1% across algorithms (as a percentage of average volume).
Bland and Altman 1986 (Lancet): limits of agreement; when differences are proportional to the mean, use a logarithmic transformation; antilogged limits are a dimensionless ratio.

Oxnard et al. 2011 (J Clin Oncol): on repeat CT within minutes (median 8 min), 3% of lesion measurements (90 lesion-reader pairs; diameters) met the RECIST progression threshold and none met partial response, without true change.

Kuhl et al. 2019 (Radiology): readers who chose identical target lesions agreed on progression in 97.7% of patients; readers who chose different target sets agreed in only 55.3% (316 patients, 3 readers).
Zhao et al. 2025: changing from diameter-based RECIST to RECIST-equivalent volume cut-offs (-65%/+73%) changed 13.9% of 2390 lesion interpretations (478 lesions, 3 radiologists).

Dahm et al. 2024: stage IV melanoma at the Tübingen centre; automated nnU-Net measurements agreed with three radiologists about as well as the radiologists agreed with each other; volumetric RECIST (-65%/+73% on volumes) differed from diameter RECIST in 7 of 58 patients.

Gong et al. 2023: applied -65%/+73% volume thresholds to summed target-lesion volumes; a per-lesion sphere model labelled more patients progressive than measured volumes (52 vs 31 of 593 at week 9); a progression call usually ends the current line of therapy.

Adhikary, Chabi and Mastmeyer 2026 (Research Square preprint v1, not peer reviewed): on Longitudinal-CT melanoma data, with expert baseline masks and a prompt-assisted longitudinal model (LongiSeg) at follow-up, the patient-level RECIST target-lesion category disagreed with the expert-mask reference in 43 of 258 patients (16.7%). Check whether the dataset is the same public Longitudinal-CT release.
Goldmacher et al. 2026: in 39 pembrolizumab trials, investigator and central review disagreed on progression in 17.7% of patients overall (n = 20,908) and 11.8% in melanoma.

Barati et al. 2026: a treatment-planning-system upgrade (RayStation) retrained deep-learning auto-segmentation models on expanded data; most structures were stable but left-lung and spinal-cord agreement fell, with one failed contour; regression tested with DSC, HD95, MSD and dose. Published online 23 September 2026.

Tomita et al. 2025 (Cureus): successive versions (VA30, VA50, VA60) of a commercial auto-contouring product (AI-Rad Companion Organs RT) changed organ contours; the rectum contour became less accurate, which the vendor documentation did not disclose.
Wasserthal et al. 2023 (Radiology: AI) describe TotalSegmentator version 1 (nnU-Net; 1204 CTs; Dice 0.943).

TotalSegmentator documentation (GitHub, accessed 12 October 2026): v2 retrained all models with more training images (1139 to 1559) and corrected labels; 'The resulting segmentations will also be slightly different from v1, because all models have been retrained'; later releases changed inference defaults and post-processing.

IAEA TRS-430 (2004) section 10.3.4: 'Compare plans performed with the new version with the same plans performed with the old version'; 'It is not sufficient to check those elements known to have changed'; section 7.7 divides vendor and user duties for software upgrades.

Huo et al. 2013 (AAPM CAD subcommittee, Med Phys): for a CAD software upgrade, sites should compare CAD results before and after the upgrade; a fixed set of test cases is recommended for acceptance testing at first installation and subsequent upgrades; recording the CAD version allows stratified analyses.

Vandewinckele et al. 2020 (Radiother Oncol): after retraining, (re)commission the model and repeat the end-to-end test; 'The reference dataset should be re-predicted on a regular basis and compared to the initial predictions during commissioning ... to verify consistency of the model'.
Hurkmans et al. 2024 (joint ESTRO-AAPM guideline): Statement 17 'Have procedures in place for upgrades and updates before clinical introduction'.

Brady et al. 2024 (multi-society statement ACR, CAR, ESR, RANZCR, RSNA): 'Another specific scenario which may require a re-evaluation of a model's performance would be the issuance of a new model version by the manufacturer.' Identify which journal version to cite (published simultaneously in several journals).

FDA, Health Canada and MHRA (October 2023), 'Predetermined change control plans for machine learning-enabled medical devices: guiding principles': a PCCP specifies planned modifications, the protocol for implementing and controlling them and the assessment of their impact; principles include methods to verify and validate changes and characterisation of the device before and after changes.

The already-cited FDA PCCP final guidance (August 2025), Appendix A item 4.c.9, asks whether patient data from previous device use will be rerun on an updated AI model and whether clinically meaningful differences before and after an update will be communicated. Verify the item number and wording.

AAPM TG-53 (Fraass et al. 1998, Med Phys 25:1773-1829): each new release of planning software requires acceptance and commissioning-type testing before clinical use; Appendix 1 divides vendor and user responsibilities for version updates. The English text was not read by the search (only a Japanese translation); verify against the English original.
Larsen et al. 2026: a mammography AI update (Transpara 1.7 to 2.1) raised AUC from 0.908 to 0.928 but 12.0% of interval cancers received a lower score.
Fehr et al. 2023 (letter): successive CAD4TB versions shifted their score scales, so a triage threshold calibrated on one version gave sensitivities from 67% to 89% across versions.

Auriac et al. 2025 (Med Phys): MOOSE 3.0.14 vs TotalSegmentator 2.0.5 on 315 patients: organ volumes within 10% for 19 of 33 organs in at least 80% of patients; 20% or more in at least a fifth of patients for four structures.
de Grauw et al. 2025 (Med Image Anal, ULS23): moving the simulated click within a lesion changed the baseline model's output, mean consistency Dice 0.787.

AccuBrain update IV1.2 to IV2.0: Dice improved (0.910 vs 0.892) yet volumes changed by a mean relative absolute error above 5% for half the measures; developers advised against mixed use (conference abstract).

Muenzel et al. 2012: with the same target lesions, measurement variability changed the RECIST category in 6.3% (same observer) to 12% (different observers) of cases, against the mean of four observers.
Seymour et al. 2017 (iRECIST, Lancet Oncol): premature discontinuation of an effective drug and continuation of an ineffective one both harm patients (verify the wording).

RCR 2024 auto-contouring guidance, section 6: 'a retrained model should be labelled with a new version number and undergo a proportionate evaluation prior to clinical use'; version information can be lost when DICOM objects move between systems.

Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 Art. 3(23) defines substantial modification; Art. 43(4) requires a new conformity assessment after a substantial modification, except pre-determined changes of systems that continue to learn after being placed on the market.
